subject: Model 2.1 latency threshold exceedance and escalation
messages:
From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmecorp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Platform OPS <ops@acmecorp.com>, sla@acmecorp.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95 spike for model 'model-2.1' in production — urgent

Marcus —

We're seeing a sharp increase in inference latencies for our production calls routed to model-2.1 starting ~2026-05-17 23:00 UTC. p95 has climbed from ~320ms to >1.2s and customer-facing requests are timing out. We've attached a small extract of p95/p50 by minute for the last 12 hours.

This is violating the SLA for ACME (p95 < 400ms) and impacting our checkout flow. Can you confirm whether any model rollout, kernel change, or quantization patch was applied in that window? We need either an immediate rollback to model-2.0 or an SLA exception/credit while we validate.

Attachments: p95_spike_20260517.csv (4KB)

Thanks,
Julia Park
Head of Platform Reliability
Acme Corp
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmecorp.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike for model 'model-2.1' in production — urgent

Julia — thanks for the heads-up and the CSV. I'm escalating immediately. Looping in Lauren (runtime lead) and Priyom (Customer Success) so we can triage and provide an action plan within the hour.

Initial ask from our side: can you confirm whether the traffic to model-2.1 is 100% of your calls, or split across a ring? Also please share any request IDs for impacted transactions if available — that helps trace across our telemetry.

We will not start any risky rollback until we align on rollback triggers and validation steps. I expect a first update by 10:00 PDT.

—Marcus
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julia Park <julia.park@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p95 spike for model 'model-2.1' in production — urgent

Quick triage summary (telemetry + infra):
- Observation window: spike begins ~2026-05-17T23:02:00Z, persists through 2026-05-18T04:30:00Z on Acme's primary fleet.
- Symptom: p50 up ~2x and p95 up ~4x. Errors are not significantly elevated (timeouts only when >1.5s).
- Correlation: a runtime kernel patch (latency-oriented micro-optimizations) rolled to canary on 2026-05-17 22:50Z then promoted to model-2.1 pool at 23:00Z. Kernel selection plus altered attention kernel scheduling appears to increase scheduler jitter for sequence lengths common to Acme's workload.

Proposed mitigation options (with risks):
1) Immediate routing of Acme's production traffic to model-2.0 variant (no code change on Acme). Fastest; zero model change but may have small behavior delta. Risk: minor model output drift vs 2.1.
2) Canary rollback of the kernel patch on the model-2.1 fleet serving Acme; validate on 1% traffic for 30 minutes then ramp. Risk: if issue is not kernel-related, could require further rollback steps.
3) Temporary SLA exception while we keep investigating (not ideal for Acme).

I attached a short rollback runbook and the SLO impact summary. My recommendation: do option 1 immediately (traffic re-route) and start option 2 as a controlled canary within 30 minutes to restore 2.1 once validated.

Attachments: runbook-rollback.txt (2KB), slo-impact-summary.pdf (8KB)

Lauren Bishop
Runtime Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia.park@acmecorp.com>, ACME Platform OPS <ops@acmecorp.com>, sla@acmecorp.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Action plan: route ACME production to model-2.0 (temporary) + canary rollback for model-2.1

Julia — thanks again. Per Lauren's triage, here's the plan we will execute immediately and will update you at each step: 

1) Traffic routing (T+5 minutes): route 100% of ACME production traffic to model-2.0 variant for requests matching your current routing key. Expected effect: immediate restoration of p95 to baseline (~<400ms). No change required on your side.
2) Canary rollback (T+30 minutes): begin rollback of the kernel patch on a small subset of model-2.1 nodes and validate against reproduced sequences. Metrics to monitor: p50/p95, tail-latency (99th), and error rates.
3) Rollback decision criteria: if after 30 min canary p95 <= 400ms and outputs pass sanity tests, we will progressively switch traffic back to model-2.1. If not, we keep traffic on 2.0 and continue investigation.
4) Customer-facing SLA: we understand this is an SLA breach window for you. We will record the incident and open an internal SLA credit review. For now, we propose a temporary operational credit while we resolve and will follow up with formal credit calculations.

We will perform steps in the order above unless you instruct otherwise. ETA for first confirmation (routing done) ~10:12 PDT.

—Marcus
From: Julia Park <julia.park@acmecorp.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Platform OPS <ops@acmecorp.com>, sla@acmecorp.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Action plan: route ACME production to model-2.0 (temporary) + canary rollback for model-2.1

Thanks Marcus / Lauren —

Routing to model-2.0 restored p95 to acceptable levels; confirmed with our monitoring. We appreciate the quick coordination. A few asks to close this loop: 
- Please document the rollback triggers that will be used before any automatic re-promotion to 2.1 (we need explicit thresholds and a timeline).
- We request a formal SLA credit calculation for the 5.5-hour impact window and an expectation for when the credit will be issued.
- Once you have preliminary postmortem notes (root cause + mitigations), please share them with our SRE team for review.

We are OK with Redwood proceeding with a canary rollback under the criteria you outlined, provided we get the trigger doc and pre- and post-validation checks.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Julia
